name: Yutenji
tagline: Shibuya in 6 minutes and Shinjuku in 16 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥90,000 to ¥100,000.
summary: The station is in Meguro City, served by Tokyu Toyoko Line. Journey times to the main business districts are 30 minutes to Otemachi, 16 minutes to Shinjuku, 6 minutes to Shibuya and 33 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥90,000 to ¥100,000. The station stands 29.8 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 9.4 m. The land around the station has gentle slopes.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 29.8 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 22.4 m to 31.8 m, a difference of 9.4 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls outside the projected inundation area. Even so, 1 of the nine points within 400 m fall inside the area, and the deepest projection there is less than 0.5 m. On the whole, the flood projection here is among the smallest in the 23 wards.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 9 clinics and 8 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 菫会目黒病院, about 10 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 総合病院三宿病院, about 13 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Tokyu Toyoko Line.
congestion: Tokyu Toyoko Line runs at 124% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch of the line is 祐天寺→中目黒, which includes this station. At 100%, the ministry's scale describes every passenger either seated or able to hold a strap or pillar. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥90,000 to ¥100,000 and 1K ¥110,000 to ¥120,000. 1LDK ¥200,000 to ¥210,000 and 2LDK ¥280,000 to ¥290,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

Whether it faces a main road or the railway

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥90,000 to ¥100,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is on the low side. a small projected flood depth and quiet surroundings pushes the figure up. On the other side, only one line, the {line}, serving the station holds it down. For 1LDK, 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: rents are lower at Yutenji, but Naka-Meguro is ahead on the number of lines and how close the centre is.
neighbours.note: About 1 km from Yutenji in a straight line. Naka-Meguro also has the Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line, which Yutenji does not. With more lines, Naka-Meguro is the better connected of the two. To Toranomon, for instance, Naka-Meguro is 7 minutes quicker. A one-room flat, though, costs about ¥28,000 more at Naka-Meguro.

neighbours.lead: Gakugei-Daigaku is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection, but Yutenji is ahead on how easy the shopping is.
neighbours.note: About 1 km from Yutenji in a straight line. It is served by the same lines as Yutenji. To Tokyo, for instance, Gakugei-Daigaku takes 3 minutes longer. Rents, flood projections and the rest differ little.

goodFor: People living alone who want to hold the rent down
notFor: People who want another route when service is suspended
People who want plenty of places to eat out
noiseSources: The nearest big road, 駒沢通り, is far enough that little traffic noise reaches the station area

leads.terrain: There are gentle slopes around the station, and which block you live on changes how much effort getting about takes.
leads.groceries: There are 9 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 1 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself is outside the projected flood area, but blocks nearby are inside it.
leads.stationNote: Only the Tokyu Toyoko Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the low side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is on the high side for the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Among the 23 wards' stations, the lines here are very lightly loaded in the morning.
leads.noiseSources: The big roads are far enough that traffic noise is unlikely to bother you.
